lyrics:
[Intro: looping orchestral string figure alone, then shuffling drums]

[Verse 1: half sung, half declaimed, over the loop]
Same grey pavement, same front door
Same face on the bus as the day before
They say you are the sum of what you've done
I've added it up and I'm still only one

[Pre-Chorus: bass enters, strings double]
And I do change
I do change
Just slow, like a coastline
Just slow, like a name

[Chorus: full band, chiming guitar, the loop continues]
So I'm gonna walk it off
Whatever it was
The year, the weight, the word I said
I'm gonna walk it off
One foot, then the other one
Till the street runs out or the feeling does

[Verse 2: over the loop, more forceful]
I talk to the kettle, I talk to the cat
I asked a pigeon once and it left it at that
There's a man in the window who looks like my dad
I nod and he nods and it isn't so bad

[Pre-Chorus: bass and strings]
And I do change
I do change
Just slow, like a coastline
Just slow, like a name

[Chorus: full band, chiming guitar, the loop continues]
So I'm gonna walk it off
Whatever it was
The year, the weight, the word I said
I'm gonna walk it off
One foot, then the other one
Till the street runs out or the feeling does

[Breakdown: drums drop out, strings and voice only]
Nobody's coming to carry me
Nobody's coming, and that's alright
I've got two good legs and an afternoon
I've got two good legs and the light

[Final Chorus: drums return, extra strings, ad-libs]
So I'm gonna walk it off
Whatever it was
The year, the weight, the word I said
I'm gonna walk it off
One foot, then the other one
Till the street runs out or the feeling does

[Outro: loop continues, vocal ad-libs, long fade]
Left, right
Left, right
Walk it, love
Walk it off
Left, right
Walk it, love
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 86 BPM, 4/4, in A with a modal, unresolved colour. A steady walking pace. Hypnotic, proud, a little weary.

VOICE: Male baritone with a nasal northern English edge. Verses are half sung and half declaimed, like someone talking to himself in the street. Choruses are fuller and more melodic. Long, loose ad-libs over the fade.

INSTRUMENTS: An orchestral string section playing one short, stately figure that repeats, unchanged, from the first bar to the last. A shuffling, loose drum beat with a strong backbeat. Deep, simple bass. Chiming electric guitar with delay in the choruses. Extra high strings and a distant bell in the final chorus. Tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the string loop alone for four bars, then the drums. 0:22 Verse 1. 0:45 Pre-chorus, bass enters. 1:07 Chorus 1. 1:35 Verse 2. 1:57 Pre-chorus. 2:19 Chorus 2. 2:47 Breakdown, drums out, strings and voice. 3:09 Drums return for the final chorus with extra strings. 3:37 Outro, the loop continues under ad-libs and fades out very slowly by 4:30.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-90s British rock with a hip-hop sense of loop and beat: wide strings, dry punchy drums, vocal slightly distant, a long fade.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The four bars of strings alone at the start. The song is recognisable before the drums arrive.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original insists nothing changes. This narrator is older and has noticed that he does change, at the speed of a coastline. The self-reliance in the breakdown is offered as good news.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Monotony, wry humour, self-acceptance, and forward motion.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

A man walks the same street he has always walked and decides that walking is the cure, for whatever it was.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: grief; anger; getting sober; getting fit at fifty; or leaving a job. 'It' is never named. Where the original says a person cannot change, this one says change is real and very slow.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: an unchanging string loop, a walking pulse, blunt lines about ordinary life, and no resolution. Designed mishearing: 'walk it off' is heard as 'walk it, love', and the outro sings exactly that.
